importantDisclaimer.title: Important Disclaimer
importantDisclaimer.sectionDescription: Important Disclaimer - Glossary of terms and calcultaions. The table below has definitions of terms used, as well as formulaes. This will help you to use standard financial terms and calculations. For example, one of the most imprortant terms are - Gross Revenue, Gross Profit, EBIDTA - are very well recognised by investors and financial professionals.
importantDisclaimer.productsPortfolioDescription: Products and Services Portfolio - list of goods or services offered by a your business. It outlines the range of offerings a company provides to its customers.
importantDisclaimer.inflationDescription: Yearly Inflation: The general increase in prices of goods and services in an economy over a period of one year. Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money.
importantDisclaimer.priceIncreaseDescription: Yearly Price Increase: The adjustment of the price list of products or services to a higher level, often due to factors like increased production costs or inflation.
importantDisclaimer.salaryIncreaseDescription: Yearly Salary Increase: Annual Salary review for employees who work for a company.
importantDisclaimer.yearlyAssumptionsOfMultipliersForEconomy: Yearly Assumptions of Multipliers for Economy Expectations

This tool helps to adjust Inflation, Price Increase, Salary Increase, and Monthly Volume on a yearly basis, considering global economic changes (e.g., war, COVID, economic crises). This might reflect assumption that economical situation stabilizes on yearly basis or declining faster.
importantDisclaimer.vatTaxDescription: VAT Tax: Value Added Tax (VAT) is a consumption tax levied on the value added at each stage of production or distribution. It is ultimately borne by the end consumer.
importantDisclaimer.pricelistExcludingVatDescription: Pricelist excluding VAT: List of prices for products or services excluding the Value Added Tax (VAT).
importantDisclaimer.costlistExcludingVatDescription: Costlist excluding VAT: List of costs associated with producing products or providing services, excluding the Value Added Tax (VAT).
importantDisclaimer.seasonalityDescription: Seasonality: Pattern of variations in business activities or sales recurring annually due to factors like weather, holidays, or consumer behavior.
importantDisclaimer.businessRumpUpOrAccelerationCurve: Business Rump Up or Acceleration Curve
importantDisclaimer.businessRumpUpOrAccelerationCurveDescrip: Business Rump Up or Acceleration Curve: Graphical representation of the level at which a business's activities (e.g., sales) increase over time. 1 (or 100%) indicates that business is fully scaled.
importantDisclaimer.targetedAudienceCrowdDescription: Targeted Audience, Crowd: Defines the intended audience for marketing efforts and business outreach. This indicator might help to understand the total Market size. Therefore might help to avoid mistakes related to unrealistically big amount of customers.
importantDisclaimer.visitorsUsersDescription: Visitors / Users: Number of people who visit, contact, book or use the business's offerings.
importantDisclaimer.customersDescription: Customers: Number of people who make a purchase from the business.
importantDisclaimer.churnAttritionRateDescription: Churn / Attrition Rate: Percentage of customers lost over time.
importantDisclaimer.clientbaseNewCustomersDescription: Clientbase New Customers: Number of new customers acquired each month.
importantDisclaimer.clientbaseLostCustomersFormula: -1 * (Previous Month Customers) * This Month Churn Rate
importantDisclaimer.clientbaseLostCustomersDescription: Clientbase Lost Customers: Number of customers lost each month.
importantDisclaimer.clientbaseLoyalCustomersFormula: Previous Month Customers * (1 - This Month Churm Rate)
importantDisclaimer.clientbaseLoyalCustomersDescription: Clientbase Loyal Customers: Number of loyal customers who consistently make purchases.
importantDisclaimer.monthlyVolumeFormula: Monthly Volume = Portfolio UnitsPerCustomer * Monthly Customers
importantDisclaimer.monthlyVolumeDescription: Monthly Volume: Quantity of products sold or services rendered in a single month.
importantDisclaimer.monthlyFreeGoodsDescription: Monthly Free Goods: Quantity of products given away as freebies or promotions.
importantDisclaimer.grossSalesRevenueFormula: Gross Sales (Revenue) = Monthly Volume * Yearly PriceList
importantDisclaimer.grossSalesRevenueDescription: Gross Sales: Total revenue generated from sales before deductions.
importantDisclaimer.discountsDescription: Discounts: Reductions in selling price to encourage sales or loyalty.
importantDisclaimer.returnsDescription: Returns: Products or services returned by customers.
importantDisclaimer.netSalesFormula: Net Sales = Gross Sales + Discounts + Returns
importantDisclaimer.netSalesDescription: Net Sales: Gross sales minus discounts, returns, or allowances.
importantDisclaimer.standardCogsDescription: Standard Cogs: Direct costs in producing goods or services.
importantDisclaimer.otherCogsFormula: Other Cogs = -1 * (Gross Sales * %GrossSales + Static Monthly Number)
importantDisclaimer.otherCogsDescription: Other Cogs: Additional costs related to production and sale.
importantDisclaimer.grossProfitFormula: Gross Profit = Net Sales + Standard Cogs + Other Cogs
importantDisclaimer.grossProfitDescription: Gross Profit: Net sales minus total cost of goods sold.
importantDisclaimer.grossProfitMarginDescription: Gross Margin: Gross profit as a percentage of net sales.
importantDisclaimer.advertisingPromoMarketingDescription: Advertising, Promo, Marketing: Expenditures to increase brand awareness, attract customers, and drive sales.
importantDisclaimer.monthlyNumberOfEmployeesFormula: List of People with their availability in percentage
importantDisclaimer.monthlyNumberOfEmployeesDescription: Monthly Number of Employees: Workforce availability for each month.
importantDisclaimer.grossSalaryDescription: Gross Salary: Total salary before deductions.
importantDisclaimer.netSalaryDescription: Net Salary - Salary for the payment to employee after taxes.
importantDisclaimer.netSalaryExpensesDescription: Net Salary Expenses: Total salary expenses after deductions and considering the number of employees.
importantDisclaimer.recruitmentCostExpenseFormula: Recruitment Monthly cost * Number of employees
importantDisclaimer.recruitmentCostExpenseDescription: Recruitment Cost: Expenditures related to hiring new employees.
importantDisclaimer.salaryTaxExpenseDescription: Salary Tax: Amount of tax deducted from gross salary.
importantDisclaimer.extraPayExpenseDescription: Extra Pay: Additional payments to employees (e.g., bonuses, incentives).
importantDisclaimer.headcountExpensesFormula: Headcount Expenses = Net Salary Expenses + Recruitment Cost + Extra Pay + Salary Tax
importantDisclaimer.headcountExpensesDescription: Headcount Expenses: Costs associated with employee compensation and recruitment.
importantDisclaimer.opexFormula: List of Monthly Expenses related to Opex Expenditures
importantDisclaimer.opexDescription: Opex (Operating Expenses): Ongoing costs to run a business, excluding production costs.
importantDisclaimer.otherIncomeLossFormula: List of estimated Uncategorised Income Loss
importantDisclaimer.otherIncomeLossDescription: Other Income, Loss: Additional sources of revenue or expenses not directly related to core operations.
importantDisclaimer.ebidtaFormula: EBITDA = Gross Profit - (Advertising,Promo,Marketing) - Headcount Expenses - Opex - Other Income, Loss - R&D
importantDisclaimer.ebidtaDescription: EBITDA: Measure of operating performance before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization.
importantDisclaimer.capexInvestmentsAcquisitionsOfFixedAsset: Capex, Investments, Acquisitions of Fixed Assets
List Of acquisitions of Assets with their Values
Capex: Investments in acquiring or upgrading fixed assets.
importantDisclaimer.amortizationAndDepreciationFormula: Same value as Capex (where amortization applicable) in total but split into monthly amortization
importantDisclaimer.amortizationAndDepreciationDescription: Amortization and Depreciation: Allocating costs of intangible and tangible assets over their useful lives.
importantDisclaimer.ebitOperatingProfitDescription: EBIT: Profit from core operations before interest and taxes.
importantDisclaimer.profitTaxDescription: Profit Tax: Taxes levied on company's profits, often corporate income tax.
importantDisclaimer.loanAndInterestDescription: Loan and Interest: Payments related to loans and interest expenses.
importantDisclaimer.netIncomeFormula: Net Income = EBIT - Profit Tax - Loan and Interest
importantDisclaimer.netIncomeDescription: Net Income: Profit remaining after deducting taxes and interest.
importantDisclaimer.totalInvestmentRequiredFormula: Total Investment Required = Capex + EBIDTA + Sum of Profit Tax + Sum of Loan Interest
importantDisclaimer.totalInvestmentRequiredDescription: Total Investment Required: Expenditures to start or expand a business, including capital investments and operational costs.

details.title: Business Plan Details
details.sectionDescription: In this section, you can set the initial input for your ideal business by providing thoughts such as the business title, intended location, and proposed opening date
details.name: Name
details.consumersRef: What are the names of consumers of goods or services?
details.currencyRef: What is a currency of this business plan simulation?
details.startDateRef: Start Date of the Plan - Estimate when you are going to start your Dream Business
details.periodMonthsRef: Period of the Plan in Months (e.g. 12 for 1 year) - represents how many Months of Business Plan do you need to calculate.
details.typeOfPlanRef: This is a type of Business plan - which can represent - Idea, Startup, or already Running Business
details.categoryRef: Category of the Plan (e.g. Business Plan, Marketing Plan, etc.)
details.yearlyInflationRateRef: Yearly Inflation Rate in your country, e.g. 5%.
details.yearlyPriceIncreaseRef: Planned yearly price increase. For best results, keep it slightly lower than inflation rate.

visitorsCustomers.title: Visitors and Customers
visitorsCustomers.sectionDescription: Imagine your ideal business has stabilized and is fully operational with customers and sales. In this section, please estimate the number of monthly visitors (for offline business) or registered users (for online businesses) that you anticipate, as well as the conversion rate of visitors into customers. This will help you to understand the potential scale of your business.
visitorsCustomers.totalMonthlyCrowdRef: Total monthly crowd thet you can expect nearby your business or visiting your online service/ facebook page, etc. This number help to understand total reachable amount of people that potentially can be interested in your services. For example, for offline coffee shop - it indicates total number of people, passing through the street or shopping mall nearby your business. You can estimate it simply by observing couple of hours traffic, and extrapolating for whole month. For Online business it might represent total number of monthly visitors (registered and not registered). For Consulting/training business - it can be total number of potential people in your area/globally who might be interested in your services.
visitorsCustomers.paidTrafficRef: Percentage of paid traffic that can you expect to have. In case of online buseness, we often buy visitors, here you can estimate approximate percent of paid trafic from previous Crowd/Unregistered visitors that we paid for. Normally this rate is extreamely low, or close to zero.
visitorsCustomers.totalMonthlyVisitorsRef: Total monthly visitors that you can expect. Number of Visitors (for offline business), Users (for online business), or registered participants (for Consulting business) - that can be estimated by observing similar busineeses and extrapolating to get montly number.
visitorsCustomers.costPerVisitorRef: Cost per visitor you expect to pay. Knowing the fact that we were heavily paying for Visitors/Registered Users, by understanding percentage of such traffic, we can set the price for each visitor (this goes to Marketing->Cost of visitors).
visitorsCustomers.monthlyConversionUserThatBuysRef: Monthly conversion rate of visitors into customers / buyers / clients. After we know how many monthly Visitors (for offline business), or Registered Users (For SaaS business) or Registered participants (for Consulting) we have, - next - we need to estimate how many of them become Customers - e.g. will pay for our services.
visitorsCustomers.totalMonthlyCustomersRef: Real Customers / Buyers. This Number is auto-calculated and represents your total montly Customers.

portfolio.title: Portfolio
portfolio.sectionDescription: In this section, outline the goods or services that you will be selling, keeping the list short but consistent. Additionally, provide accurate predictions of the cost of goods and the retail/final price for each item. This will help you assess the financial aspects of your business and plan your pricing strategy effectively.
portfolio.useShareConversion: Use Share conversion customer that buys
portfolio.numberOfMonths: Number Of Months for Initial Stock
portfolio.brandRef: Your brand under which your products are presented
portfolio.productNameRef: This is List of your Product and/or Services.
portfolio.costPriceRef: Cost Price of one item or service. It includes the cost of the raw materials, labor, and overhead costs associated with producing the goods. It is also known as the cost of sales or cost of goods.
portfolio.priceRef: The price of a product or service is the amount of money that a consumer pays for it. It is the amount of money that a business receives in exchange for the sale of its goods or services.
portfolio.productMarkupRef: The markup is the difference between the cost of a product and its selling price. It is expressed as a percentage of the cost. For example, if the cost of a product is $100 and the selling price is $150, then the markup is 50%. Value is auto-calculated.
portfolio.productMarginRef: The margin is the difference between the cost of a product and its selling price. It is expressed as a percentage of the selling price. For example, if the cost of a product is $100 and the selling price is $150, then the margin is 33.33%. Value is auto-calculated.
portfolio.eachNCustomerBuysRef: Each N-Customer that buys product or service. For example, if we sell coffee and tea, we can say, that out from 3 cusomers, 2 buy coffee, and 1 buys tea. It means - each 3rd buys tea, and each 1.5th buys coffee. Expectedly, if we divide 1/byNEachCustomer - we will get weight of sales - 1/3=33% tea and 1/1.5=67% coffee respectively.
portfolio.shareCustomerThatBuyRef: This is percentage of customers by product from total number of customers. Please note, sum by product can be larger than 100% and therefore larger than total customers. This is expected. For example, customer can buy a coffee and a tiramisu, which will indicate that same customer bought 2 items from portfolio.
portfolio.monthlyCustomersRef: Total Number of monthly customers who buy our products. Please note, sum by product can be larger than total number of customers . This is expected. For example, customer can buy a coffee and a tiramisu, which will indicate that same customer bought 2 items from portfolio, therefore he will be twice in products, and once in total.
portfolio.ordersMonthPerCustomerRef: Number of orders*units per customer per month. For example we can estimate that normally each customer buys not single capcake but few normally, therefore, it makes sense to indicate 2.5 capcakes per one cheque.
portfolio.totalUnitsRef: Total number of units sold per month.
portfolio.estimatedFailedOrdersRef: The percentage of orders that are not fulfilled due to various reasons such as the customer changing their mind, the product being out of stock, or the customer not being able to pay for the product.
portfolio.standardDiscountRef: Average total The percentage of discounts that we give monthly to our customers
portfolio.onFirstInitialStockRef: If you are selling a physical product, then you will need to buy the product from a supplier and store it in a warehouse.
portfolio.totalAssetValueRef: The total value of all assets owned by a business.
portfolio.beginningMonthsRef: The number of months that you will need to pay for the initial stock. For example, if you need to pay for the initial stock in 3 months, then the number of months that you will need to pay for the initial stock is 3.
portfolio.yearlyInflationRateRef: Yearly Inflation Rate in your country, e.g. 5%.
portfolio.yearlyPriceIncreaseRef: Planned yearly price increase. For best results, keep it slightly lower than inflation rate.
portfolio.overrideFromBusinessDetailsRef: Override Inflation, Price Increase, UOM by yourself
portfolio.numberOfMonthsForInitialStockRef: How many months you need to gain first sell
portfolio.ammortisationOrDepreciationRef: How many months one asset will serve

costPrice.title: Cost list & Price list
costPrice.sectionDescription: In the table below you can see and compare on yearly basis your portfolio cost of goods or services (cogs) and price-list taking into consideration specified earlier inflation rate and yearly price increase.
costPrice.costHeader: Cost prices of goods or services

seasonality.title: Seasonality
seasonality.sectionDescription: In the table below you can specify seasonality impact, for example -50% - half of expected sales, 200% - double sales during the month. Defalult value is populated 100% - indicates no impact on sales at all.

acceleration.title: Acceleration
acceleration.sectionDescription: So called 'rump-up' curve - is a simple prediction based on common similar business type - how much time does it takes for similar business to stabilize in this area. It also includes personal suggestions of when sales are started, or if we know that sales already happening, what is an approximate level of expected sales in comparison to 'stabilized business', for example 30%.
acceleration.estimatedScale: And .. Estimated scale of business on month number

headcount.title: Headcount and Payroll
headcount.sectionDescription: Data in this section represents monthly number of employees, as well as cost associated with their payroll.

crowdTargetedAudience.title: People Crowd / Targeted Audience
crowdTargetedAudience.sectionDescription: Below data represents potential maximum targeted audience, or so-called Crowd - maximum number of people that your business can reach. It is calcualted as Targeted Audience from 'About Customer Section' and multiplied by seasonality. It is expectedly equal by product and in total, just because - those audience are not yet our customers and they can be associated with any product or business in total.

visitors.title: Visitors / Users
visitors.sectionDescription: Below data represents number of visitors or users associated with your ideal business. It is calcualted as Number of Users  from "About Customer Section" and multiplied by Seasonality and multiplied by Acceleration rump up. It is expectedly equal by product and in total, just because - those audience are not yet our customers and they can be associated with any product or business in total. Its just Visitors / Users who contacted or declared a wish to Buy or Subscribe to Our Services.

customers.title: Customers
customers.sectionDescription: Below data represents number of Customers who buy our Prosucts. It is calcualted as Number of Customers from Portfolio and multiplied by Seasonality and multiplied by Acceleration rump up. It is expectedly completely vary across products, and might not match total business customers. This is because, certainly we might expect Customers who buy several Products from our Portfolio, but it will be same Customer in total number of customers that our business serves.

volume.title: Monthly Volume
volume.sectionDescription: Below data - represents Sales Volume, which indicates an amount of Goods or Services sold. It is calcualted as Number of Units Per Customer from Portfolio and multiplied by Number of Customers from Previous Table. It is obvious, that in the Portfolio you was making an assumption for number of Units Monthly, therefore here at the month where you expect 100% rump-up of your business, you will get an exactly same number that stated in portfolio, with a difference adjusted by Seasonality. You can sum up those numbers to get total sales data for your ideal business.

discountsAndReturns.title: Discounts & Returns
discountsAndReturns.sectionDescription: Below data - represents Discounts and Returns, which indicates an amount of Goods or Services sold. It is calcualted as Number of Units Per Customer from Portfolio and multiplied by Number of Customers from Previous Table. It is obvious, that in the Portfolio you was making an assumption for number of Units Monthly, therefore here at the month where you expect 100% rump-up of your business, you will get an exactly same number that stated in portfolio, with a difference adjusted by Seasonality. You can sum up those numbers to get total sales data for your ideal business.

netSales.title: Net Sales Revenue
netSales.sectionDescription: Below data - represents Net Sales, which indicates an amount of Goods or Services sold. It is calcualted as Number of Units Per Customer from Portfolio and multiplied by Number of Customers from Previous Table. It is obvious, that in the Portfolio you was making an assumption for number of Units Monthly, therefore here at the month where you expect 100% rump-up of your business, you will get an exactly same number that stated in portfolio, with a difference adjusted by Seasonality. You can sum up those numbers to get total sales data for your ideal business.

otherCogs.title: Other Monthly Cogs
otherCogs.sectionDescription: Here you can list all possible cost related to your portfolio to make it avaliable and exposed to the customer. Few examples are - Customs Clearance, Logistics, Certification, Glowes and Sanitation, Royalty, any other cost which is not Operating Expendenture, but can be closely associated with goods or services avaliable for the customer.

grossMargin.title: Gross Margin
grossMargin.sectionDescription: Gross Profit and Gross Margin - are important indicators which indicate exact part of your revenue which reamins after deduction of the cost associated with product manufacturing and exposing it to the customer.

investmentAndCapex.title: Investments & CAPEX
investmentAndCapex.sectionDescription: Below data - represents Capital Expenditures, which is full list of investments for your business - such us buying land, house, equipment, fllet and machinery, cimputers, initial stock, initial rent deposit, and more.

marketing.title: Marketing
marketing.sectionDescription: Data in this section represents monthly expenses related to marketing, sotial media, promotion, etc.

opex.title: Opex
opex.sectionDescription: Data in this section represents common monthy operating expenses, such as utilities, electricity, rent payment, insurances, travel expenses, fuel, fleet expenses, etc.

rnd.title: RnD
rnd.sectionDescription: Data in this section represents operating cost dedicated to Research and Development. Its not applicable for most of businesses, however still if you want to spend some cost to develop and experiment this is a proper way to reflect it.

otherincomeloss.title: Other Operating Income Loss
otherincomeloss.sectionDescription: Data in this section represents any operating cost which may or may not happen with a certain level of probability. Often its called Sundry. Examples of such cost are - sundry, stolen property, force major, unexpected downtimes, electricity failures, extreme weather conditions, crimes, penalties, unexpected entertaiments, charity, unexpected donations, presents, deposit transfers, etc.

ebidta.title: EBIT Operating Profit
ebidta.sectionDescription: In this section you ccan make a full assumptions about EBIDTA - Earnings Before Interest and Taxes. One one of the main indicators of a business.
